company.name: ThreeFlow
company.shortDescription: ThreeFlow is an employee benefits software that allows brokers and carriers to manage the entire placement process.
company.description:
ThreeFlow is a Benefits Placement System, a new category of enterprise software that allows brokers and carriers to manage the entire placement process in one shared system. They make it easier for carriers to win business and brokers to empower employers with the details they need to make benefits selections. By connecting people, systems, and information, they enable easier communication, a quicker process, and better decisions making busy people more productive. 

ThreeFlow was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in Chicago, IL, USA.

productsAndServices.description: A software platform that enables brokers and carriers to manage the entire employee benefits placement process, including renewals, new business RFPs, analysis, negotiation, and implementation.

productsAndServices.description: A tool that enables real-time collaboration between brokers and carriers to analyze benefit line items, compare quotes side-by-side, and access quote history.
productsAndServices.name: Digital Analysis and Negotiation

productsAndServices.description: A system to collect, schedule, and manage benefits renewals according to preferred timelines and workflows.
productsAndServices.name: Renewal Management

productsAndServices.description: An analytics tool providing brokers and carriers with real-time data on market activity, carrier response rates, new business premiums, and other metrics to inform revenue planning and competitive analysis.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Series C round raised $30,000,000, or 35.58% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $50,151,118 to $309,336,322, a 6.17x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

caveats: Crunchbase does not expose the complete weighting behind these proprietary scores.
